problem_sources.text: ﻿AGENTIC AI HACKATHON Aerophilia 2026 — Technical Event Rulebook EVENT SUMMARY Agentic AI Hackathon challenges student teams to design and build autonomous AI agents that can plan, use tools, and act toward a real objective — not just answer prompts. Teams pick one problem track, architect an agent that reasons, calls tools, and completes multi-step tasks with minimal human hand-holding, and demo it live to a panel of judges. Winning teams will receive prizes worth ₹15,000. REGISTRATION & ELIGIBILITY TEAM REQUIREMENTS * Each team must have 2 to 4 members. * Open to all college students with a valid college ID. * Participants may only be part of one team. * Each team must designate one member as captain for all communication with organizers. REGISTRATION * Registrations are open on the official Aerophilia website (aerophilia.in). * Registration fee: ₹400 per team, payable at the time of confirmation. * Teams must submit their problem track choice and tech stack at registration. ________________ PROBLEM TRACKS Teams must build their agent around ONE of the following tracks: * Claims Triage Agent (Insurance) — Reads incident/claim submissions and returns a severity, coverage, and fraud-risk assessment, routing to the right handler. * Client Intake Agent (Legal/Professional Services) — Runs structured intake conversations, screens against criteria, and books qualified consultations. * On-Call Incident Agent (Engineering) — Investigates an alert using logs/deploys/traces and proposes a diagnosis and fix for human approval. * Shopping Assist Agent (Retail) — Answers pre-purchase questions (fit, compatibility, stock) using product data rather than marketing copy. * Portfolio Health Monitor (Wealth/Investing) — Tracks holdings against news/filings and flags changes with supporting evidence, without giving trade advice. Teams may adapt a track's scenario with mock/sample data — real customer or financial data must not be used. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS * The submission must demonstrate a planning → tool-use → action loop, not a single-shot prompt-response. * Any framework is allowed: LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, or a custom build. * Use of AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor) during the hackathon is allowed — disclose usage in the README. * At least one external tool/API call (search, database, calculator, file, or similar) must be part of the agent's flow. * Participants should come prepared to showcase their work; the event focuses on demonstrating existing builds rather than on-spot development. JUDGING CRITERIA Criteria Weight Description Agentic Architecture 30% Quality of planning, tool use, and autonomous decision-making Technical Execution 25% Working demo, code quality, robustness Problem Fit & Impact 20% How well the agent solves the chosen track's real-world problem Innovation 15% Originality of approach or use case Presentation 10% Clarity of demo and explanation to judges SUBMISSION & SCHEDULE * Event Date: 14th November 2026 * Venue: CSE Central lab, Ground floor, Main block * Teams must submit a public GitHub repo with a README and a 2–3 minute demo video as a fallback for live demo failures. * Live demos are capped at 5 minutes per team, followed by 3 minutes of judge Q&A. * Submission deadline: Project repositories and videos must be submitted prior to the showcase round to facilitate the live demonstration. * The problem statement will be released 10-15 days before the event CODE OF CONDUCT & TERMS * Harassment, plagiarism, or use of another team's codebase will result in immediate disqualification. * Teams retain ownership of their code; organizers may showcase winning projects with credit. * Any changes to rules will be communicated via registered email and the Aerophilia website. * Decisions of the judges and organizers are final and binding. CONTACT INFORMATION Naren S J: +91 82968 33381 Tharun Rai: +91 63608 29990
